findings.title: Trailing slash stripping is inconsistent with path handling
findings.body: The new line strips trailing slashes from the cookie path (line 213), but the existing path handling logic (lines 210–212) already normalizes paths by cutting everything from the last slash to the end. This creates two different ways to handle trailing slashes, which violates the custom rule on naming consistency and local conventions. The trailing slash stripping should be removed to align with the existing path handling logic.

findings.title: Shared cookies are sent without domain/path validation
findings.body: The new code sends shared cookies (domain='', path='') unconditionally (lines 266–268), bypassing the domain and path matching logic that follows. This violates RFC 6265 and can expose cookies to unintended origins. Shared cookies should only be sent if they match the request's origin and path, not unconditionally.

findings.title: Cookie filtering logic is inefficient and incorrect
findings.body: The new filtering logic (lines 287–291) uses `itertools.product` to generate all (domain, path) pairs and then filters cookies from those pairs. This is inefficient and can produce incorrect results because it does not respect the original cookie storage structure (`self._cookies` as a `defaultdict`). The logic should iterate over the stored cookies directly and apply the matching rules per cookie, as the original code did.

findings.title: Edge case handling for cookie path trailing slashes is unclear
findings.body: The new edge case handling (lines 299–301) checks if the cookie path is longer than the request path, which is a confusing way to handle trailing slashes. This logic should be clarified or merged with the existing path matching logic to avoid confusion and maintain consistency with the rest of the codebase.

summary.problem: The changes to cookie filtering and path handling introduce correctness issues, inefficiencies, and inconsistencies with existing conventions.
summary.done_well: The refactoring attempts to improve path and domain matching logic, and the removal of the unused import is a minor improvement.
